correctness.rationale: Exact DFT interpolation gives the full normalized moment cone and strict interior. A rational arithmetic script proves all 1953 positive-index nodal inequalities and their sign reversals for degrees N<=62; an all-N midpoint estimate based on |(sin t/t) double prime|<=1/3 and a rigorous Si(3pi/2) enclosure proves overshoot for every N>=63. Abel summation plus integration by parts verifies the limiting extremum. Continuous positive-mass inputs have mean strictly within (-pi,pi); smooth nonnegative endpoint bumps supply infeasible examples below the threshold. Code and all necessary files are embedded.

originality.rationale: Cai–Lin–Lin 2023 supplies nodal Fourier positivity and strict feasibility hypothesis (H3); the classical Fourier sawtooth supplies partial-sum and Gibbs tools. The assessed original output is the exact universal strict-feasibility degree 63 for (mass, first raw moment), established by exhaustive finite rational inequalities and an all-degree analytic bound. Compared with the accessible 76 prior numerical-analysis claims and eight semantic mathematical-record queries; no covering implication was located. This is a qualified self-review, not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: For a published positivity-and-moment-preserving Fourier optimization problem, its Slater-type hypothesis determines whether numerical projection exists with all positive nodal values. The result identifies the exact degree 63 ensuring feasibility uniformly over all real nonnegative physical data for the natural (mass,raw first moment) pair, and constructs smooth admissible failures below it. This resolves a method-level, physically motivated feasibility cutoff rather than an arbitrarily chosen Fourier coefficient or a generic Gibbs restatement. It is limited to 1D and two moments.
